stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
stories.author: Amin Saberi
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of stealth biases in Large Language Models (LLMs) used in high-stakes applications.
These biases can be introduced anywhere in the LLM supply chain and are dangerous because they only manifest on specific topics.
The proposed method, 'Cartridge Distillation,' aims to expose these hidden preferential biases, which can transfer even across unrelated data.

stories.title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation

stories.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video

bullet_points: Introduces 'World from Motion,' a method to generate freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian representations from single-camera video input.
The technique conditions a video model using dense, pixel-aligned renderings to accurately encode appearance, geometry, and 3D motion.
A key innovation is using aligned multiview video pairs to train the model, enabling correction of rendering artifacts and filling in missing scene data.

A key finding suggests that a single Transformer layer can achieve performance comparable to training with a full set of parameters in RL.

stories.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
stories.author: Arman Cohan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current LLM evaluations by measuring the distance between LLM-generated research ideas and human-generated ones.
A novel evaluation framework is introduced, which reverse-engineers prior works from high-quality human research papers to establish baselines.
The research aims to characterize how closely LLM ideation aligns with the inspiration and trajectory of actual human scientific breakthroughs.

stories.title: Language-Critique Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations

bullet_points: Proposes a novel language-critique framework for imitation learning.
Addresses the limitation of traditional methods that use only scalar supervision signals (e.g., confidence scores).
Allows the model to leverage natural language to express intermediate reasoning about task progress and failures from suboptimal demonstrations.

stories.title: Theoria: Rewrite-Acceptability Verification over Informal Reasoning States
stories.author: Michael Saldivar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Theoria,' a new verification architecture designed to bridge the gap between formal proof assistants and LLM judges.
Theoria addresses the limitations of current AI verification methods: formal proofs lack coverage, while LLM judges are opaque and unauditable.
It works by rewriting candidate solutions into typed state transitions, each requiring an explicit, justifiable license.

stories.title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis

bullet_points: Proposes the 'state-prediction separation hypothesis' for Transformers.
Suggests that separating the token prediction function from the state storage function improves language modeling.
Introduces a novel Transformer variant with two computation streams to test this separation.
